KEY MESSAGE 1...A warm front will move north through the region 
tonight, followed by a strong cold front that will pose the threat 
of severe weather on Friday afternoon and evening. 

Low pressure developing over the Midwest this afternoon will lift 
northeast into the Great Lakes tonight and into southern Quebec on 
Friday. As the system lifts north, a warm front will lift north 
through the region overnight. As forcing for ascent increases along 
with increasing moisture advection, occasional showers and periods 
of rain are anticipated to develop and spread into the area after 
midnight. Cannot rule out some embedded thunder overnight as well, 
as there is some elevated instability present in forecast soundings. 
Showers and some patchy fog will continue through about daybreak, 
before the warm front lifts clear of the area by late morning. There 
should then be a lull in activity through early afternoon.

Once the region is in the warm sector, expect a few hours of mostly 
sunny conditions on Friday under warm and moist southwest flow. 
Forecast highs are expected to be in the mid 70s to low 80s across 
much of eastern PA and NJ with highs possibly topping out in the mid 
80s across the Delmarva. Dew points will also rise into the mid to 
upper 60s in the afternoon. 

By mid to late afternoon, focus will be to the west as a strong cold 
front trails to the west. Convection by this time should already be 
ongoing across portions of NY and western PA tracking east toward 
the area. Forecast guidance currently depicts a narrow corridor of 
instability where MLCAPE is around 500 J/kg, perhaps up to 1000 J/kg 
over western areas. While instability is meager at best, strong 
background wind fields aloft will be coincided with bulk shear 
values in excess of 50 kt along the immediate front. As a result, 
the Storm Prediction Center has increased wind probabilities across 
the entire forecast area, now being placed into a Slight risk (Level 
2/5) for severe weather on Friday. The primary hazard is damaging 
wind gusts given the overall set-up, however cannot entirely rule 
out a brief spin-up as well. Timing appears to around 4-6 PM for 
western areas, 6-8 PM around the I-95 corridor, and 8-10 PM for 
coastal areas and across the Delmarva. With diurnal heating ceasing 
this time of year much earlier than in peak summer, it is expected 
that the squall line will be losing steam in intensity as it 
progresses further east. Showers and storms will clear the area from 
west to east later Friday evening.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Widespread frost and freeze conditions are 
increasingly likely Saturday night.

The trough axis shifts east away from the region and high pressure 
builds in at the surface for Saturday Night. This will result in 
some of the coldest air of the season to date settling in over the 
entire area. Skies will clear out by sunset on Saturday, with winds 
gradually diminishing through the night. The elevated winds, 
especially south and east of the I-95 corridor, will prevent 
temperatures from bottoming out completely though. So, while we will 
have decent radiational cooling conditions, it won't be perfectly 
ideal. Ended up lowering temperatures a few degrees under the NBM 
though. 

As a result, low temperatures are expected to fall below freezing 
across the Poconos and northwestern NJ. Freezing temperatures could 
extend down through the I-78 corridor though, with the current 
forecast for Reading/Allentown having lows around 33 to 34. Rural 
areas even across southeastern PA and southern NJ cannot entirely 
rule out seeing their first freeze of the year either. For the rest 
of the area, lows in the mid 30 to upper 30s are expected, with 40s 
along the coast. 

Elevated winds and a dry airmass may actually preclude frost 
development, especially along the I-95 corridor and points south and 
east. There is a scenario where we see temperatures in the mid 30s 
but no widespread frost given how dry the airmass will be. However, 
the first widespread hard freeze looks increasingly likely for the 
Poconos and northwestern NJ. Headlines are going to follow in 
subsequent forecast updates.

Temperatures moderate from Sunday onward. Temperatures on Sunday 
Night north of Philadelphia will drop into the mid to upper 30s, but 
some areas may no longer need frost/freeze headlines beyond Saturday 
Night. After that, lows each night for most of next week should be 
above 40 degrees where the growing season is still active. Dry and 
tranquil conditions are expected with no significant weather hazards 
anticipated at this time for next week.
